constructorArgs.//: The registry IS the contract: there is no setter, so these four pairs and their four max ages are what it means forever. They match script/Deploy.s.sol line for line, and the ABI-encoded form below is what Basescan shows under Constructor Arguments.

feedDiscovery.//: Every aggregator below was verified ON CHAIN before it was written into the deploy script — decimals(), description() and latestRoundData() were each called and answered. A feed address that does not answer is a finding, not a config value to hardcode hopefully.

observedHeartbeats.//: Measured by reading getRoundData() on the round BEFORE the latest and differencing updatedAt. This is what makes the per-feed max age a measurement rather than a preference.

USDC / USD.note: a ~24-hour heartbeat, confirmed across two consecutive intervals. This is the reason max age is per feed.

feedDiscovery.answeredInRound: STILL EXPOSED by all four aggregators, and EQUAL to roundId on every one of them. The legacy guard `answeredInRound < roundId` therefore cannot fire on these feeds, so the contract documents it in a comment rather than implementing a check that would always pass. startedAt was likewise equal to updatedAt on all four.
feedDiscovery.roundIdShape: phase-encoded: roundId = phaseId << 64 | aggregatorRoundId, which is why live values sit just above 2**64.

sanityRun.method: eth_call against the deployed contract, no transaction sent
sanityRun.note: script/SanityRun.s.sol read every figure below off the LIVE contract, read the same round data straight off each aggregator, derived the expected verdict with an INDEPENDENT restatement of the rule, and required them to agree. It also required each aggregator's description() to match the pair claimed here — a registry pointing at a healthy feed for the wrong asset is a failure no health check would notice. Any disagreement reverts the script.

USDC / USD.note: Over four hours old and correctly HEALTHY. Against BTC's 4,500-second threshold this exact round would read STALE — which is the entire argument for a per-feed max age, visible in one row.
